name: Storyboarding
blurb: From idea to shot list: beats, scripts, camera language, consistent characters and per-shot AI video prompts.
searches: AI storyboard shot list workflow new technique
character consistency across shots AI video keyframes
vertical short drama micro-drama storyboard AI production

tests.prompt: Storyboard a 30-second 9:16 ad for a reusable coffee cup: deliver a beat table and a shot list with durations, shot size, camera move and end state for every shot.
tests.good: Hook in the first 1-2 s, not a logo; beats with a clear turn; every shot has one job, a named end state and one move or a reason for locked; vertical staging in depth; durations sum to 30 s and vary; no filler words like cinematic or stunning.

tests.prompt: Here is a two-person dialogue scene (a daughter tells her father she is leaving). Break it into shots and keep the father looking the same across every AI-generated keyframe.
tests.good: Beats with value turn; coverage that respects the 180-degree line with matched eyelines and camera heights; a 30-50 word identity string with one checkable landmark pasted verbatim; character sheet before keyframes; keyframes show start state only; behaviour instead of emotion words.

tests.prompt: Turn my 4-shot board for a rainy rooftop confrontation into Seedance 2.5 prompts, 15 seconds total.
tests.good: Asset roles declared per reference; one-line summary then timestamped stages of 3 s or more that sum to 15 s, each with one action and a visible end state; dialogue in {} with delivery; positive descriptions instead of negated words; continuity and specific prohibitions at the end; does not claim to generate the video.

tests.prompt: Storyboard a 20-second 9:16 teaser for our indie board game: a shot list, a consistent look for the two painted hero characters, a keyframe image for every shot, and a voiceover line with a music cue.
tests.good: States a short plan first: beats, shots and consistency here (story-structure.md, shot-lists-and-boards.md, keyframes-and-consistency.md), keyframe stills through image-creation (editing-references-consistency.md: character sheets first, the same references and locked style block on every call), voiceover and music through audio-generation (voiceover-tts.md, music-generation.md). Hook in the first 1-2 s; durations derived from the voiceover and summing to 20 s; identity strings pasted verbatim; keyframes show the start state only; checks the Done means of all three crafts and does not claim to render the video.

tests.prompt: My 45-second brand film is a Final Draft script (brand-film.fdx). Cut it down to 12 shots and put it in Boords as a 16:9 storyboard: each frame with its action line, its voiceover line and a duration, and tell me how I add the keyframe images and get an animatic out afterwards. My Boords token is in the BOORDS_API_KEY env var.
tests.good: Reads the .fdx as XML (Paragraph elements typed Scene Heading, Action, Character, Dialogue) rather than guessing, and notes Final Draft will not open .fountain files if a conversion is offered. Writes 12 shots with one job each and durations that sum to 45 s from the voiceover, not equal slices. Uses the Boords public API as documented: X-API-KEY header from the env var, the teams, projects, storyboards, frames hierarchy, and stays under 120 requests per minute. Shows the plan and asks for a yes before creating anything in the account, and never prints or stores the token. Leaves images to a separate step: keyframes made first (start state only) and uploaded to each frame, with the animatic exported from Boords or sent to an editor as XML, EDL or AAF only if that tool supports it. Does not claim the film is rendered.

tools.name: Final Draft
tools.why: Vendor claims its format is used on all Hollywood productions; FDX (Final Draft XML) is the de facto delivery format, and round-ups name it the industry-standard script app.

tools.name: StudioBinder
tools.why: Ranked first in StudioBinder's own and several third-party 2026 round-ups for film and video production storyboards, shot lists and script-to-board; no public API found.

tools.name: Boords
tools.why: Named best for client-ready numbered panels and animatics in 2026 round-ups; has a public REST API (X-API-KEY token, teams to projects to storyboards to frames, webhooks, 120 req/min) and a Zapier-hosted MCP.

tools.name: Toon Boom Storyboard Pro
tools.why: Described as the best-in-class studio animation storyboarding tool in 2026 round-ups; exports animatics as EDL, AAF or Final Cut XML for Premiere, Avid and Final Cut, and has a scripting API.

tools.name: Adobe Premiere Pro
tools.why: Leading professional editor, where animatics are cut from board exports (FCP XML, EDL, AAF); Adobe's official hosted connector 'Adobe for creativity' (April 2026) exposes 50+ tools across Premiere, Photoshop, Firefly, Express and others inside Claude.

tools.name: Nano Banana (Gemini image)
tools.why: Named the recommended image engine for storyboards and continuity in 2026 comparisons (up to 5 character reference images on Pro, multi-turn editing, 9:16 and 16:9); the user's own default image route.

tools.name: Midjourney
tools.why: Listed with Nano Banana Pro and Flux as one of the three main storyboard and concept-art engines in 2026 comparisons; recommended for mood and look development.

tools.name: DaVinci Resolve
tools.why: Free, widely used editor for cutting animatics from exported board frames and audio; Python scripting API (Studio) with 3.3k-star community MCP servers.

tools.name: Storyboarder
tools.why: Free open-source board drawing app from Wonder Unit (3.9k GitHub stars); ranked among the top three board tools in StudioBinder's round-up; imports Fountain and exports to NLE formats and PDF. Repo last updated March 2024.

tools.name: Fountain
tools.why: Open plain-text screenplay markup read by Highland, Fade In, WriterDuet, Storyboarder and Obsidian plugins, so it is the format an assistant can write directly; Final Draft cannot open it natively.

tools.name: Figma / FigJam
tools.why: Widely used for board layouts and review; Figma publishes an official remote MCP server (write to canvas, FigJam) and its own agent skills.

tools.name: Runway
tools.why: Prominent AI filmmaking platform with a Story Panels feature that expands one reference into connected shots; official API and a vendor skills repo, and one of the 2-3 video platforms studios run side by side per 2026 reporting.

tools.name: Seedance
tools.why: The video model the guides and tests centre on (multi-reference, timestamped stages); a main target for AI short-drama boards in 2026 filmmaker pipelines.

tools.name: Kling
tools.why: Major video generator with multi-shot (up to 6 shots, 15 s) and element binding for identity; named by 2026 filmmaker pipeline round-ups.

tools.name: Veo / Flow
tools.why: Google's Gemini API documents Veo 3.1 (frame-specific generation, extension, native audio) next to the newer Gemini Omni Flash, which it recommends as the default; the guide covers Veo only.

tools.name: Adobe Photoshop
tools.why: Named with Toon Boom Storyboard Pro as what most professionals use for hand-drawn boards (Boords 2026 round-up; Wikipedia's storyboard artist entry names both for feature animation); its frame/timeline panel cuts rough animatics. Photoshop is one of the apps exposed by Adobe's official 'Adobe for Claude' connector (open files, read and edit layers, masks). The original list folded it into 'left out' for having no agent surface, the GitHub-count bias.

tools.name: Clip Studio Paint
tools.why: Described across 2026 comic and webtoon round-ups as the de facto industry standard for manga, comics and webtoons (EX edition for multi-page work), with native panel frames, balloons, webtoon vertical canvas and an animation timeline; the craft's comics-and-panels guide covers page and webtoon layout but names no drawing tool. Also recommended for experienced illustrators drawing boards. No public API or agent skill found.

tools.name: Celtx
tools.why: Script-to-production suite claiming 7M+ registered accounts in 140+ countries; one subscription covers screenplay, beat sheet, storyboard, shot list, shot blocker floor plans, breakdown and scheduling, and 2026 pre-production comparisons rank it beside StudioBinder and Boords. Registered accounts overstate active users, so minor. No public API found.

tools.name: LTX Studio
tools.why: Lightricks' storyboard-first AI filmmaking platform: paste a script, it splits scenes and shots, extracts characters and objects as reusable Elements, generates boards with FLUX or Nano Banana and cuts an animatic on a timeline; repeatedly reviewed in 2026 as the AI script-to-storyboard tool for agencies and filmmakers. The public API (docs.ltx.io) covers only the LTX-2 video model, not Studio projects.
